title: ci: add signed artifact + provenance pipeline and release manifest for private deployments
author: Maya Chen
release_notes: Added a signed artifact build+provenance pipeline, generated signed release manifests for private deployments, and integrated Helm/Terraform release steps. No breaking changes for existing installers; rollout controlled via feature flag.
description:
Context and motivation: Private and on-prem installs must have verifiable, audit-friendly release artifacts for regulated customers. This PR introduces a CI/CD pipeline that builds installer artifacts (tarballs, Helm charts, Terraform module packages), produces cryptographic signatures and SLSA-like provenance attestations, and publishes a signed release manifest used by the private installer/upgrader. This enables customers to verify origin and integrity of artifacts during air-gapped or VPC installs.

What this PR does (high level):
- New GitHub Actions workflow .github/workflows/release-artifacts.yml: builds artifacts for linux/amd64 and linux/arm64, packages Helm charts, and runs chartmuseum packaging.
- Artifact signing using cosign: supports both keyless (recommended) and KMS-backed keys for enterprise installs. Signatures and attestations (.sig and .att) are uploaded alongside artifacts.
- Provenance: generates a minimal in-toto/SLSA attestation (producer, build-recipe, materials, buildType, invocation) for each artifact and embeds hashes in the release manifest.
- Release manifest: artifacts/releases/private-release-manifest-v{version}.json produced and signed. The manifest contains artifact URLs, checksums, attestations links, recommended upgrade order and rollback hints for multi-component upgrades. The private installer now validates the manifest signature before applying upgrades.
- Helm and Terraform integration: charts are packaged and pushed to our chart repo; a versioned terraform module archive is created and published to the private-artifacts bucket with matching provenance. The manifest includes module versions used for upgrades.
- Upgrade/rollback tooling: added manifests metadata for canary percentage, health-check probes to run during rollout, and a 'rollback-sequence' array to prefer safe revert order for dependent services.
- CI checks: chart lint, helm unit smoke, terraform fmt & validate, terratest (light), artifact signature verification, and manifest signature verification as part of release workflow.

Files changed (high level):
- .github/workflows/release-artifacts.yml (new)
- ci/scripts/build_artifacts.sh (new)
- ci/scripts/sign_and_produce_attestation.sh (new)
- installer/release/manifest-generator.py (new)
- helm-charts/private/Chart.yaml and values (packaging and provenance fields)
- terraform/modules/private-installer/module.tf (versioning/publish hooks)
- docs/operational/release_process.md (doc updates)
- tests/ci/verify-signatures.sh (new)
- packaging/Makefile (updated)
- .circleci/config.yml (minor pipeline skip adjustments)
- package.json (devdep bump for chart lint)
- scripts/upgrade-hooks/rollback-order.yaml (new metadata)

Commits (summary):
- initial: add release workflow and helper scripts
- add cosign signing and keyless flow with fallback to KMS
- produce in-toto-style attestation and attach to artifacts
- manifest generator with signed output and schema v1alpha1
- hook installer validation and tests for manifest verification

Test plan / CI:
- Unit: manifest-generator unit tests run in CI.
- Integration: a release workflow run in the fork CI (dry-run) that builds a candidate release and publishes to staging bucket. Terratest runs a light create/destroy for the terraform module in the CI account.
- Signature verification: verify-signatures.sh checks cosign sigs and attestations for staging artifacts.
- E2E (manual gated): an on-prem smoke upgrade test using staging artifacts to validate installer acceptance of signed manifests.

Security notes:
- The pipeline supports cosign keyless mode (fulfilling sigstore recommendations) to avoid long-lived private keys in CI. For enterprise customers we also support using KMS/HSM-backed signing; kms key paths are read from secrets and never stored in repo.
- The verifier rejects manifests with missing attestations or mismatched checksums.
- We added a small opt-in feature flag PRIVATE_RELEASE_VERIFY_SIG to the installer so customers can enable strict enforcement. The default behavior in this PR is permissive for existing customers to avoid accidental failures; enforcement will be flipped on after a one-cycle migration window.

Rollout strategy and migration:
- Initial rollout: enable workflow for candidate releases and push to staging bucket. Installer will accept signed manifest but not require it by default.
- After validation and a 2-week bake period we will flip PRIVATE_RELEASE_VERIFY_SIG to strict in a follow-up PR and announce in the release notes.

Backward compatibility:
- Existing unsigned artifacts remain consumable while permissive mode is on. The manifest generator can produce unsigned manifests when invoked with --allow-unsigned (used only for internal legacy flows).

Review conversation (highlights):
- Rajat Kapoor: "Security nit: please ensure KMS key material never appears in workflow logs and rotate example keys in docs."
- Maya Chen (author): "Added redaction in the workflow and moved example key specs to docs/operational/keys.md; CI secrets are required for KMS mode."
- Elena Park: "CI: terratest is timing out in the initial run — can we run a lighter terratest or move full test to a nightly job?"
- Maya Chen: "Switched to light mode in PR CI and added nightly/full-e2e job to release pipeline."
- Samir Patel: "Can we add a signature verification unit to the installer so we can run it in local dev?"
- Maya Chen: "Added tests/ci/verify-signatures.sh and an installer flag --verify-manifest for local runs; documented in release_process.md."
- Rajat Kapoor (approved): "LGTM pending final CI green and docs updates."

CI history: initial run failed on chart lint and an accidental circleci skip; I fixed Chart.yaml fields and bumped helm/chart-testing devdep. Re-ran workflow and all checks passed (chart-lint, terraform-validate, terratest-light, signature-verify). Final release workflow run signed artifacts and produced manifest in staging.

Follow-ups and known TODOs:
- ENG-7311: integrate SLSA invocation detail enrichment from builder (future PR).
- Add QA playbook for offline verification in air-gapped environments (docs/operational/airgap-verification.md).
- Automate rotation of cosign for KMS-backed keys across accounts (separate ticket).

Merge strategy: squash and merge. This PR was squashed into a single commit with the message: "ci(release): signed artifacts, provenance, and release manifest for private deployments (ENG-7283)" and merged into main.

Impact and why it matters: This gives enterprise customers a verifiable chain-of-custody for installer assets, reduces risk for regulated deployments, and opens the path for stricter enforcement of artifact provenance for higher assurance installations.
